speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) what are the reasons driving the number of wild boar attacks on residents in Bukit Panjang; (b) what is the current estimate of the wild boar population in Bukit Panjang based on the most recent assessments conducted by the relevant authorities; and (c) what measures are implemented thus far by NParks to manage the growing wild boar population in Bukit Panjang and ensure the safety of residents in densely populated residential areas.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) what are the causes for the recent wild boar attacks in Bukit Panjang; and (b) what further measures are needed to prevent wild boar attacks and ensure the safety of residents living near nature reserves.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) what are the actions taken by NParks when the public reports wild boar sightings at the residential neighbourhoods; (b) whether the current number of wild boars at the nature reserves are at an ecologically sustainable level; and (c) what further measures and plans are there to manage the population of wild boars.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Members have asked about what the National Parks Board (NParks) is doing to manage Singapore's wild boar population and to ensure public safety.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We want residents to feel safe in and around our green spaces.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: That is why we take a proactive, holistic and science-based approach in managing the wild boar population.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Wild boars are naturally found in many parts of the world, including Singapore and our region.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: For the most part, wild boars travel in herds and stay within forested areas.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: While Bukit Panjang and the adjacent Zhenghua Nature Park do not have a resident wild boar population, wild boars appear from time to time due to the estate's close proximity to nature reserves and other forested areas, such as Chestnut Nature Park and Dairy Farm Nature Park.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We know that residents in Zhenghua and Bukit Panjang are concerned about the recent wild boar incidents in the area.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: NParks has taken steps to mitigate the risks and will be closely monitoring the situation.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: NParks is also working closely with the grassroots and the Holland-Bukit Panjang Town Council to engage the community on proper food waste management to reduce human-generated food sources that may attract wild boars.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Wild boars have high reproductive rates, giving birth up to twice a year with a litter size of up to 12 piglets.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Female wild boars can start reproducing from 18 months of age.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Wild boars also do not have natural predators in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: NParks, therefore, has to actively manage the wild boar population.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: This includes carrying out habitat modification, such as removing oil palms to reduce wild boars' food sources.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: In line with the practice in many other countries, NParks also removes boars where necessary to ensure public safety.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: NParks is also working closely with stakeholders on public education and outreach, to promote safe and responsible human-wildlife encounters.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: This includes discouraging the feeding of wildlife, which can alter their natural foraging behaviour and cause them to rely on humans for food.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: NParks does this through public education as well as enforcement action against illegal feeding of wildlife.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: NParks is also engaging the community on how to respond to wildlife sightings, such as remaining calm and keeping a safe distance if they encounter a wild boar.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: When a member of the public reports a wild boar sighting, NParks will respond immediately.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: NParks will continue to take a comprehensive science- and community-based approach to manage Singapore's wild boar population and to ensure public safety.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Can I ask the Senior Minister of State how effective has that been?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: And in the case of Bukit Panjang, we have a very lengthy border with the nature reserve and nature parks, so whether that is actually possible to exclude wild boars from coming in.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: The second question is, as the Senior Minister of State also mentioned about the high reproductive rate of the wild boars and that there being no natural predators, how is NParks going to ensure that the population growth of the wild boars will not cause damage to the ecosystems within the nature parks and whether the nature parks, indeed, have the space to accommodate so many wild boars?

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: These have been effective in restricting the wild boars' access to the fenced areas.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: In some areas, NParks has also deployed cattle grids, which are metal grates designed with gaps that are wide enough for the feet of hooved animals, such as wild boars, to enter.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: This deters such animals from crossing the grid, whilst still allowing people to cross.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: NParks will continue to monitor the efficacy of these measures, moving forward.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: On Mr Liang Eng Hwa's second question, I would like to share with the Member that NParks carries out tracking studies to monitor changes in the wild boar population and to identify hotspots.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Based on NParks' findings, the wild boar population in Singapore's nature reserves has remained relatively stable.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: These densities are lower than those recorded in larger tracts of forest reserves in the region with similar vegetation types.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: As I shared in my earlier reply, NParks will continue to take a comprehensive science- and community-based approach to manage Singapore's wild boar population.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: This includes conducting habitat modification to reduce their food sources, managing their movements through fencing and hoarding, and removing wild boars where necessary to ensure public safety.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We will also continue to discourage the feeding of wildlife and take enforcement action against such acts.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Deputy Speaker, I would like to ask the Senior Minister of State was the presence of a dog in the latest incident at Zhenghua Nature Park a contributing factor to the incident?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And the second supplementary question is, if the wild boar population is left unmanaged, what is the impact to our biodiversity?

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: For dog owners who walk their dogs in parks that are near forested areas, we encourage them to avoid walking their dogs at night due to the low visibility and the possibility of encountering nocturnal wildlife.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: If a dog owner sees a wild boar in the distance while walking his or her dog, the owner is advised to keep the dog close by tightening its leash and to move away from the wild boar as quietly and rapidly as possible.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: On the Member's second question on the ecological role of wild boars, as I mentioned earlier, wild boars are indigenous to many parts of the world, including in Europe, parts of Asia, in Singapore and the region.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: They do serve important ecological functions, such as acting as seed dispersers and helping with soil nutrient recycling with their rooting behaviour.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: They eat not just vegetation, but they also dig up soil to eat the small worms and insects under the soil.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Their feeding behaviour helps to have a positive impact on the ecosystem by dispersing seeds.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, in this way, they can help to regenerate native flora.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Boars also compete aggressively with other species for food.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: But at the same time, I think we look at two extreme suggestions that have been raised by different people.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: But on the other hand, it is also impossible to not have any wild boars in Singapore at all, not least because within our region, there are many wild boars outside of Singapore and they can swim to Singapore as well.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, our approach is a proactive one, using a science- and community-based approach to manage wild boars and to maintain the balance in our ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But could I also ask what is the carrying capacity of our forests for wild boars in Singapore and also whether NParks has the projected carrying capacity as we develop more forested areas?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But could the Senior Minister of State clarify how it would be science-based if we are really basing it on complaints?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: When there are complaints, we go in and remove a few wild boars.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: And we benchmarked them with some of the comparable densities that we found in the region of similar tracts of land and similar vegetation.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: It is something for which we have to find a balance.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: On the Member's second point about how effective it has been, I also mentioned earlier in my reply how we measure their density and look at comparisons around the world.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I am not saying that we are perfect or that we have found the answers.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: This is an issue that does not just confront Singapore.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Many other jurisdictions, many other countries that we speak to beyond Asia, in Europe as well, face the same problems and challenges.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We are constantly working with them, understanding what they do and updating our playbook here.
